claims.text: The coupled wear-corrosion response of high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of a stable passive oxide layer.
A stable passive oxide layer reduces metal dissolution.
A stable passive oxide layer reduces wear-induced damage.
An alloy with a stable passive oxide layer will exhibit lower total degradation than an otherwise matched alloy without such a layer.
An alloy with a stable passive oxide layer will exhibit a lower wear component of degradation than the baseline.
An alloy with a stable passive oxide layer will exhibit a lower corrosion component of degradation than the baseline.
The prediction should hold for high-entropy alloys that form stable passive oxide layers.
The prediction may fail for alloys with unstable or non-passive oxide layers.
Alloy composition may influence passive-oxide formation and stability.
Alloy microstructure may influence passive-oxide formation and stability.
Oxide-layer stability can be varied in a controlled tribo-corrosion comparison while measuring wear rate, corrosion rate, and oxide thickness and composition.
An increase in total degradation with a stable oxide layer, or failure of both degradation components to decrease as predicted, would falsify the hypothesis.
